prompt: A company switches its inventory costing method from FIFO to weighted-average cost during a period of rising prices. Compared to FIFO, this change will most likely result in:

options.A: Lower COGS, higher ending inventory, and higher net income.
options.B: Higher COGS, lower ending inventory, and lower net income.
options.C: Higher COGS, lower ending inventory, and higher net income.

explanation: When prices are rising, FIFO assigns older (lower) costs to COGS and newer (higher) costs to ending inventory. Weighted-average spreads costs evenly, resulting in a higher COGS (relative to FIFO) and a lower ending inventory balance. Higher COGS means lower gross profit and lower net income. Option A describes FIFO relative to weighted-average, not the other way around. Option C is internally inconsistent — higher COGS cannot produce higher net income, all else equal.
